text:
Leah Mendoza: Quick check on Billing > Account form validation patterns. I prototyped a flow where tax fields are conditionally required and the form lives in a wide panel. Options: (1) inline-on-change showing errors as users type with a small persistent 'Required' hint; (2) submit-summary toast with links to fields (keeps UI clean but risks discoverability); (3) inline-on-blur + summary fallback for small viewports. Main concerns: screen reader order, keyboard-only users, and not hiding tax/legal errors behind a toast. Arun Patel: Inline-on-blur + touched semantics is my +1. Tax fields can be tricky and users expect immediate context. Toasts are easy to miss during keyboard flow or when browser chrome hides them. Diane Kowalski: Agree with Arun. Also we need clearer required markers for compound fields (e.g., address block). Instead of per-input asterisks, maybe a group-level 'Required' label plus per-field aria-required where applicable. Kai Morgan: Implementation note: backend returns errors as map keys like "billing.address.zip". We'll normalize to data-field-id="billing-address-zip" so anchors are deterministic. If we do a summary, it must move focus to the summary and announce the count, then links should move focus to the field and the field should be announced. Leah Mendoza: Good. Copy preferences: inline messages must be specific: "VAT ID is required for EU companies" vs generic "Invalid input". Summary header: "3 fields need attention" with each list item like "VAT ID Fix". Synth (a11y-bot): Checklist: 1) inline errors use role=alert OR aria-live=assertive; 2) summary uses aria-live=polite and receives focus (tabindex=\"-1\"); 3) focus order tested with screen readers; 4) group-level required labels exposed to SR; 5) color contrast for error text >= 4.5:1. Arun Patel: Small ARIA snippet we can reuse in the pattern doc: ```
VAT ID is required for EU companies
``` This ensures an immediate announcement. Diane Kowalski: Destructive confirmation debate: when a customer cancels a paid plan we discussed typed-confirm vs modal+checkbox vs banner with final steps. My view: require typed-confirm for plan cancellations that immediately stop billing or delete invoicing history. For downgrades or pause, modal+undo is sufficient. Typed-confirm wording: "Type CANCEL to immediately stop billing for this account." Kai Morgan: Dev note: typed-confirm should be case-insensitive and trimmed. Also include a data-test-id for e2e. For the modal flows, provide an undo window and an API flag for scheduled cancellations. Leah Mendoza: UX nit: show the typed-confirm input in monospace and autofocus it, include aria-describedby that spells out consequences. Also show an inline summary of what will be deleted or retained. Synth (a11y-bot): Typed-confirm accessibility reminders: link label+input with for/id, describe consequences via aria-describedby, announce result with role=status, and ensure keyboard-only users can cancel easily. Arun Patel: One more: for compact mobile we should default to inline messages but hide long explanatory copy behind a more link that expands. That keeps density but maintains SR access. Diane Kowalski: Acceptance criteria request: add keyboard-only reproduction, VoiceOver and NVDA read-order checks, and a unit test that maps server error keys to DOM anchors. Leah Mendoza: Proposed decision: default to inline-on-blur (touched), reserve space to avoid layout shift, show concise summary banner on submit for very long forms or tiny viewports, typed-confirm required for immediate-billing cancellations, modal+undo for non-critical deletes. I'll update the Patterns doc with ARIA snippets, copy examples, and the server-field-id mapping. Any objections? Arun Patel: No objections. Kai Morgan: No objections; I'll add the server mapping to the API spec. Synth (a11y-bot): Logging accessibility follow-up: A11Y-7833. Checklist appended to the Patterns doc. Leah Mendoza: Thanks all I'll post Figma mocks and the spec link after lunch. End thread.
